title: Anthony Morris to James Monroe, Cadiz, Seville and Madrid, 1814-15: thirteen coded texts in the State Department code (the = 1385) with its sixteen blocks in reverse order (NARA M31 roll 14, catalogue 650); with three letters of W. C. C. Claiborne to Madison, 1805-06 (NARA T260), in a copy with the same reversed blocks (in progress)

steps.what: WAINUT contribution: NARA M31 roll 14 frames 0036-0039 fetched; frame 0039 (page '4', code with clear phrases in lines 1-6) chosen to work on.
WAINUT contribution: frame 0039 transcribed from the full frame and enlarged crops, lines 1-6 and 10-12 first, then lines 7-9 and 13-26: 554 groups in 26 lines.

WAINUT contribution: 220 number-to-value tables from the repository (main and open WAINUT pull requests) applied directly to the groups and scored on function words: none fits (best function-word share 0.11).

WAINUT contribution: constant shifts of the group numbers, with and without a modulus, against the US tables: the JQA table at +1100 stands out (function-word share 0.25 against 0.03 for the next tables) because one block of 100 lines up.

WAINUT contribution: best JQA offset for each Morris block of 100: the busy blocks give +1500, +1300, +1100 (Morris 1-300), which suggests the sixteen blocks in reverse order (block_map.tsv); the first round overstated this as a clean pattern in every block. On the corrected transcription function words alone pick that block for 8 of 16 Morris blocks (1-300, 401-500, 601-700, 801-1100); the other eight follow from the pattern and from context.

WAINUT contribution: a second agent re-read 144 groups blind from the image (140 agree) and re-applied the method with its own code. The three clear misreadings it found (L9 724 -> 721 dem, L9 131 -> 13 ad, L24 108 -> 608 or) each turn a broken syllable into the expected one (democratic, administration, ambassador). It corrected overstated counts of the first round: 76.285 'of the' 15x (not 25x); 'territory' and 'insurrection' 2x each as identical group strings (not 3x).

WAINUT contribution: decode.py --controls on the 552 groups: block_map.tsv coverage 0.917, function words 0.353; identity 0.630 / 0.058; 20,000 random orders of the 16 blocks: function words median 0.062, 99.9th percentile 0.250, max 0.297. Per block, against word bigrams of Ford, Writings of JQA vols 3-4, the block_map.tsv block ranks first (one tie) for 15 of 16 Morris blocks; Morris 1501-1600 ranks second (3 bigrams against 4) and is kept from the pattern and from context (should, United States, Minister).

WAINUT contribution: frame 0039 written out as sentences (morris1813_reading.md): 506 of 554 groups have a table value; read_share 0.678 (research/reading_audit/v2_score.py hole rate 0.322); 670 read [?Floridas] from context at all five occurrences; names Jefferson, Madison, Baton Rouge from the table syllables.

WAINUT contribution: one web search and two by the verifier found no printed decipherment and no record of the code with reversed blocks. Manning (1925) vol. 3, Woolfley and the HSP Morris papers not checked.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents: 68 frames of M31 roll 14 fetched around the coded frames catalogue 650 left open; the copies identified as Nos. 18, 19, 24, 25 and 28 (frame 0139 is the coded part of No. 19, not of No. 18); a wholly coded document on 0115-0116 and three coded lines on 0111 found and not read.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents: numerals of the five letters (1,035 groups) transcribed from full-resolution crops before decoding, with no key open, and their hashes frozen; copies collated where they exist. The No. 25 numerals were transcribed after the clerk's decipherment of another copy (frame 0174) had been seen.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents: decoded with beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv under the block reversal (beling/scripts/decode650.py) and written out as sentences with the mark rules of PR #200. Read share over coded groups: No. 18 0.981, No. 19 0.955, No. 24 0.980, No. 25 1.000, No. 28 1.000 (beling/scripts/read_share.py). Context readings: 145 = relative, 131 = re, 1569 = United States; 593.813, 575.1060 and [370] unread.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents: key-only decode against clerks' decipherments on other copies (share of the clerk's letters matched in order; 200 shuffled keys, seed 650; beling/scripts/score_interlinear.py): No. 24 vs frame 0196 0.904 (shuffled best 0.342, median 0.215); No. 25 vs frame 0174 0.945 (best 0.343, median 0.201). Neither is blind: 0196 was glimpsed at low resolution before transcribing and its dark text read after decoding; 0174 was seen before transcribing.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents: Woolfley (2013) searched for the five letters, first by Google Books snippets, then in full text on Ebook Central: coded passages of Nos. 18, 19 and 24 are quoted (Ebook Central pp. 98-100, 106), agreeing with the decode apart from three word differences in No. 18; Nos. 25 and 28 not found. Manning vol. 3 and two web searches found nothing. American State Papers and Papers of James Monroe vol. 7 not checked.

Andrew Beling, with AI agents (PR #200; recorded here on 12 Nov 2026 from beling/README.md): a surviving sheet of the State Department code (NARA M97 roll 13 frames 1056-1057, printed by Weber as WE028) transcribed in full (beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, 1,600 entries, seven blank, eleven disputed) and used under the block reversal; letters of 4 and 11 April and 11 May 1814, 27 January and 24 March 1815 transcribed (two readers on the first four) and read; frame 0039 dated to 4 January 1814 and reread with its clear copies in view.

Independent verification of PR #415 before integration: the three scripts read and re-run, the five line-by-line decodes byte-identical; an independent decoder written from the key CSV alone agrees on all 1,035 groups; the 1,600 rows of the reversal column agree with the block formula; the two clerk tests reproduce (0.904 and 0.945; shuffled best 0.342 and 0.343); all 205 groups of No. 24 compared with frame 0220 at full resolution and agree (the last is 1551 or 1557, as flagged); frames 0112 and 0139 sampled; frames 0113, 0221, 0209, 0210 and the other copies not viewed. The order of work (numerals frozen before decoding) rests on the contributor's record: one commit.

Integration: each of the ten letter readings read as sentences against its decode and a reading review recorded. Words that the groups do not give were marked as inferences where they were not: 'liberal' and 'liberality' (li-er-al) in No. 18, 'approbation' (ap-pro-bat-ad) in No. 19. All letters recounted by one rule (word_share.py): 0.972, 0.946, 0.962, 0.958, 0.943, 0.977, 1.000, 0.957, 0.977, 1.000. No. 19 and No. 13 fall under 0.95. In No. 24 the opening 593.813 is compared with 598.813 = Sir at the head of 24 March 1815.

The contributor's follow-up commit c84e484c to PR 415, after the integration: his own reading reviews (grade A) of the five catalogue 650 letters, 'actu[al]' marked as supplied in No. 28, 'office' noted as read by the stroke rule in No. 19, and the opening 593.813 of No. 24 left as numbers. His 593.813 stays a hole as the integration's [?Sir]; his reviews are recorded with the integration reviews.

Integration: both decoded with beling/scripts/decode650.py, unchanged key. Frames 0115-0116 are a copy in Spanish of Pedro de Cevallos's note to Morris, Palacio, 20 November 1814, spelled with the English code's syllables; read as sentences and translated (0.962). Integration: two web searches (the Cevallos note; the No. 24 Council of State sentence with American State Papers). No printed text of either found. One result summarises an annotation in the Papers of James Madison (Founders Online, Madison/03-08-02-0355): Erving's letter to Monroe of 4 December 1814 enclosed a copy and translation of the Cevallos note; the page could not be opened here. Claiborne letters (then targets/claiborne1806): Image 0226 (T260 roll 7, end of 24 Oct 1805) compared group by group: the 57 live groups agree with claiborne/transcription.txt except the second Lakes, 153 1482L -> 153 148L (the final hook read as a 2, as on 0225; added to claiborne/transcription_corrections.tsv). Before 'of' (76) the clerk wrote 362 285 (';' 'the'), then struck 153 148L 1 12 (an eye-skip to 'Lakes a few' two lines below); 'collecting' has no group: Wagner's gloss supplies it. With the correction claiborne/we028_check.py gives 295 of 328 words mechanically (was 294); by hand 319 of 328 (was 317): the second Lakes and 'the' now fit, 'collecting' joins the encoder slips.

Claiborne letters (then targets/claiborne1806): Entry 1077 = tra: in Beling's transcription both halves of the M97 r13 sheet read tra, and the block runs tol, ton, too, tor, total, toward, town, tra, trac, tract, traction (WE028 570-580), so tro cannot stand at 1077 in alphabetical order; WE028 has no tro or troop entry at all (tre 854, tri 856, tru 857 in Morris numbering). Morris uses 1077 for con-tra-ry (No. 18, 20 Sep 1814) and writes troops as 1519 (trouble, cut back by strokes) + 603 op. Claiborne's clerk wrote tro- as 1077 tra three times: a consistent substitution of the nearest syllable, not a misread of the sheet. The sheet image itself was not re-read here.

Claiborne letters (then targets/claiborne1806): Letters of 18 and 19 Nov 1806 (Library of Congress, Burr Conspiracy Collection; NARA T260 roll 8 image 0408 is a typed slip saying they were removed there). texts.label: Morris to Monroe, Cadiz, 4 January 1814 and enclosed proposal, M31 roll 14 frame 0039 (page '4'), catalogue 650

reading_review.note: Read as sentences: coherent with scattered holes. The page starts and ends mid-sentence, and the digit rereads behind it were made by agents with the clear text in view (beling/frame39/frame0039_rereads.md).

texts.summary: The end of Morris's cover letter of 4 January 1814, signed in code: the US should keep a force near Florida against the British, and a change in the Regency would help them. Then the start of the proposal he enclosed, whose allegations are its author's: that Jefferson and Madison worked to separate Spain's American colonies, instigated the West Florida insurrection, seized Baton Rouge and encouraged the revolutionaries of Caracas.

texts.label: No. 12, Cadiz, 4 April 1814, M31 roll 14 frames 0082-0083 (second copy 0087-0088)

reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the line-by-line decode: coherent, with three inferred words and the unread sign after two full stops.

texts.summary: East Florida might be bought on moderate terms, partly paid in produce of the United States, but only with presents or douceurs of perhaps ten thousand dollars; Morris is still waiting at Cadiz for a reply to his proposal.

texts.summary: Morris means to go to Madrid shortly, to be nearer the source of authentic information; he has not heard from Monroe since reaching Europe and acts on his own discretion.

texts.summary: Detained at Seville on the way to Madrid as the king returns: the fear that he will not take the oath to the constitution; and Morris blames the failure to free the American captives at Algiers on an agent he distrusts.

texts.summary: After nine pages in clear on the king's return, Morris ends in code: in this unexpected state of things he thinks it best to stay quiet until he hears from Monroe.

texts.label: No. 18, Seville, 20 September 1814, M31 roll 14 frames 0112-0113 (copies 0117-0118, 0129), catalogue 650
texts.summary: The Inquisition restored in July against the wishes of all the ministers, through the king's confessor and the papal nuncio; the Cortes' decrees on the tobacco and other monopolies repealed; arrests, discontent and disturbances at Cadiz; benevolences and forced loans; the king in the arms of the nobility and clergy; no change on Florida and Louisiana; Casa Yrujo reported as the next secretary of state.

texts.label: Pedro de Cevallos to Morris, Palacio, 20 November 1814, a copy in Spanish put into the code, M31 roll 14 frames 0115-0116 (copies 0169-0170, 0201)

texts.summary: The Spanish secretary of state answers Morris: the king resents the conduct of the United States, the appointment of Erving does not repair the refusal to recognise the minister Spain sent in 1809, and satisfaction must begin with that recognition; even so, Morris may deal with Cevallos on matters between the two states.

texts.label: No. 24, Madrid, 30 December 1814, M31 roll 14 frame 0220 (copies 0205, 0196), catalogue 650
texts.summary: From a source he trusts: the Council of State is preparing a report to the king recommending a declaration of war on the United States over Louisiana and Florida; 47,000 soldiers and 5,000 officers back from France, at least 160,000 under arms, and two expeditions of ten thousand fitting out at Cadiz for Mexico and Buenos Aires, to sail early in January.

texts.label: Madrid, 24 March 1815, M31 roll 14 frames 0124-0125 and 0191-0193

reading_review.by: integration review of PR #415 (a model reading, not a person)
reading_review.note: The longest letter; read as sentences throughout, with inferred words bunched in one sentence on those shut out of employment. One reader in PR #200.

texts.summary: No change in relations with Spain; Erving's instructions about the new secretary of legation, Brent, who left Madrid for Valencia; then a long account of discontent under Ferdinand VII: palace favourites, arrests and exiles, the ayuntamientos of 1807 restored, a treasury that cannot pay the army.

texts.label: No. 28, Madrid, 12 May 1815, M31 roll 14 frames 0209-0210, catalogue 650
texts.summary: Things stand as on 24 March; with no communication with the government since Erving's letters he has had no talks with the secretary of state, but the result at New Orleans must have changed the court's views.

texts.label: Claiborne to Madison, New Orleans, 24 October 1805, 13 January and 25 November 1806: the coded words decoded with the code sheet for checking against the decipherment of the time, NARA T260 roll 7 images 0224-0226 and roll 8 images 0045 and 0409 (in progress)
texts.summary: Claiborne reports Spanish troops arriving at Pensacola and ordered to Baton Rouge and Mobile and asks that the forts be strengthened and gunboats stationed (1805); gives the strength of the regular troops at New Orleans and an order of General Wilkinson (January 1806); and writes that a conspiracy injurious to the United States is formed, with persons of high standing concerned (November 1806).
texts.note: A mechanical decode shown for checking, not a new reading: the text of these letters is Jacob Wagner's decipherment of the time (claiborne/decryption.txt, lined up with the groups in transcription.txt). The coded words are scattered words and phrases inside letters otherwise in clear. read_share is the share of Wagner's words that the code sheet under the reversal gives by a mechanical rule, all three letters: 295 of 328. Per letter: 228/250 (0.912), 40/51 (0.784), 27/27 (1.000). With a hand classification 319 of 328. Not pooled with the Morris texts.
